_comment: Hand-identified functions of ffxiv.exe (the 2013 beta client), applied by Rhipper's ghidra/ApplyFacts.java after the RTTI names (rtti32.py), so these win. One entry per function: the name, and the evidence.

0x403aa0.name: WinMain
0x403aa0.evidence: ___tmainCRTStartup calls it as (0x400000, 0, its command-line pointer, STARTUPINFO.wShowWindow): hInstance, hPrevInstance, lpCmdLine, nShowCmd

0x420900.name: GetMyDocumentsPath
0x420900.evidence: SHGetMalloc, SHGetSpecialFolderLocation(0, 5 = CSIDL_PERSONAL), SHGetPathFromIDListW into its string argument, the item list freed through IMalloc::Free; its caller appends "/My Games/"

0x408da0.name: MD5Init
0x408da0.evidence: sets the state to 0x67452301 0xefcdab89 0x98badcfe 0x10325476 and the 64-bit bit count @0x10 to 0

0x40b1f0.name: MD5Update
0x40b1f0.evidence: adds len*8 to the 64-bit count @0x10 (carry into @0x14), buffers into @0x18 and runs MD5Transform on each 64-byte block

0x40a9b0.name: MD5Transform
0x40a9b0.evidence: MD5's round functions and constants (0x242070db, ...) over one 64-byte block; MD5Update calls it per block

0x40b2a0.name: MD5Final
0x40b2a0.evidence: pads with the 0x80 block @0x12fc5d0 to 56 mod 64, appends the 8-byte count, writes the 16-byte digest, resets the context to MD5Init's values. Run under emulation with MD5Init/MD5Update it gives the standard MD5 digest

0x409a70.name: BlowfishInit
0x409a70.evidence: copies the pi tables (P[18] @0x12fac88 = 0x243f6a88..., S[4][256] @0x12facd0) into a 0x1048-byte object, XORs the key into P cycling over it, then fills P and S by encrypting a zero block chained. Key bytes are read as signed char and ORed in sign-extended

0x40d1d0.name: BlowfishEncryptBlock
0x40d1d0.evidence: 16 Feistel rounds with P[0..15] and F = ((S0[a]+S1[b])^S2[c])+S3[d], then P[17]/P[16]; on one (L, R) pair by pointer. BlowfishInit's schedule calls it

0x407e80.name: BlowfishEncrypt
0x407e80.evidence: (src, dst, len): copies src to dst, then BlowfishEncryptBlock's rounds over each 8-byte block as two little-endian u32; with a zero key and block gives Schneier's 4EF99745 6198DD78 (emulated)

0x407f40.name: BlowfishDecrypt
0x407f40.evidence: BlowfishEncrypt's rounds with P[17] down to P[2], then P[0]/P[1]; inverts BlowfishEncrypt (emulated)

0xe377b0.name: LobbyCryptEngine
0xe377b0.evidence: the constructor: sets LobbyCryptEngine's vftable, zeroes +4..+0x30 and the Blowfish pointer @0x30, sets +4 = 0x12345678 and +0xc = 1000 (ServiceConsumerConnectionManager's constructor inlines the same at +0x88)

0xe36880.name: WriteEncryptionInit
0xe36880.evidence: vtable slot 1: copies "Test Ticket Data" into +0x10, sets +8 to time() if zero, writes them to the segment it is given at +0x34 and +0x74 (payload 0x24 and 0x64 of the client's type-9 segment, as captured)

0xe38140.name: ReadEncryptionReply
0xe38140.evidence: vtable slot 4, called by DispatchSegment for segment type 10: MD5 of the engine's +4..+0x30 (0x2c bytes) is the key of a new 0x1048-byte Blowfish kept @0x30; decrypts the 0x280-byte payload of the 0x290-byte segment and writes a 0x38-byte type-2 segment from its u32 @0 and 32 bytes @0xc

0xe369b0.name: Encrypt
0xe369b0.evidence: vtable slot 6: BlowfishEncrypt in place on (data, len & ~0x1f) with the Blowfish @0x30, when there is one

0xe369e0.name: Decrypt
0xe369e0.evidence: vtable slot 7: BlowfishDecrypt in place on (data, len & ~0x1f) with the Blowfish @0x30; ReadSegment calls it on each IPC segment's payload

0xe39a70.name: ServiceConsumerConnectionManager
0xe39a70.evidence: the constructor: sets ServiceConsumerConnectionManager's vftable, builds a LobbyCryptEngine in place at +0x88 and points +0x80 at it

0xe393a0.name: DispatchSegment
0xe393a0.evidence: reads one segment with ReadSegment (passing the crypt engine @+0x80) and switches on its type: 1 and 2 to their handlers, 7 sets a flag, 9 to the engine's slot 2, 10 to the engine's slot 4 (ReadEncryptionReply) and then AcceptConnectionId

0xe392e0.name: AcceptConnectionId
0xe392e0.evidence: for a connection whose id (+4) is still 0 and a type-2 segment whose u32 @0x10 is not 0: stores that u32 as the connection's id and calls the connected callbacks (this's slot 3, the owner's slot 3)

0xe37c10.name: ReadSegment
0xe37c10.evidence: inflates the frame (InflateFrame), takes the segment at the read offset (from 0x20) and switches on its u16 type @0xc: 1/2 copied only at size 0x38, 7/8 at 0x18, 9 at 0x278, 10 at 0x290; 3 (IPC) copied to a 0x8c8 buffer and decrypted through the crypt engine's slot 7

0xe36cf0.name: InflateFrame
0xe36cf0.evidence: when the frame header's byte @0x19 is 1: inflates the body after the 0x20-byte header (zlib uncompress, up to 0x1000 bytes), copies it back, clears @0x19 and sets the size @0x10 to 0x20 + the inflated length

0xe39ed0.name: ClientPacketBuilder
0xe39ed0.evidence: the constructor: sets PacketDataBuilder's, PacketBufferTmpl's and then ClientPacketBuilder's vftables, sizes the buffer (its 2nd argument) and keeps the opcode (its 1st) @0x30; every lobby operation builds its request with it (opcode 5 size 0x100, 3 size 0x28, 0xb size 0x1f0, 4 size 0x30, as the client sends them)

0xe3b8f0.name: Dispatch
0xe3b8f0.evidence: vtable slot 1: reads the u16 opcode @2 of the IPC header and calls slot 2..13 for 1, 2, 0xc, 0xd, 0xe, 0xf, 0x10, 0x15, 0x16, 0x17, 0x1f4, 0x1f5 with the body (+0x10)

0xe46940.name: WriteRequest
0xe46940.evidence: vtable slot 0: per step builds 0x1f5 / 5 / 6 / 0x1f6 and stores the opcode it waits for (0x1f5, 0xc, 0xc, 0x1f5); opcode 5 carries 0x6e0000 @8, 0x1347 @0xc, the session id @0x10 and "ffxiv.exe/<size>/<sha1>" @0x50, as captured

0xe45ec0.name: ReadReply
0xe45ec0.evidence: vtable slot 1: 0xc goes to ReadServiceAccountList and then the done callback; 0x1f5 checks @0x14/@0x1c; any other opcode fails the step (@0x10 = 4)

0xe46e80.name: WriteRequest
0xe46e80.evidence: vtable slot 0: builds opcode 3 (0x28 bytes: sequence @0, flags @9, the service account id @0x10, which the client sent back as 1 after a list giving id 1) and waits for 0xd

0xe47070.name: ReadReply
0xe47070.evidence: vtable slot 1: 0x15 to ReadServerList, 0x16 and 0x17 read and still waiting, 0xd to ReadCharaList and, on its last page, the done callback (0xe3e940)

0xe47160.name: WriteRequest
0xe47160.evidence: vtable slot 0: builds opcode 0xb (0x1f0 bytes): content id @8, the step @0x19 (|0x80 while more chunks follow), world id @0x1a, name @0x1c, the CharaMake JSON in 400-byte chunks @0x3c; waits for 0xe. Seen: step 1 with world 1 and the name, step 2 with the content id answered to step 1 and {"classid":118,"classname":"CharaMake",...}

0xe45f40.name: ReadReply
0xe45f40.evidence: vtable slot 1: for 0xe switches on the step @0xa of the body (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7), each through ReadCharaMakeReply and then its own callback; 0x17 to the retainer reader

0xe46f70.name: WriteRequest
0xe46f70.evidence: vtable slot 0: builds opcode 4 (0x30 bytes: sequence @0, the character's content id @8) and waits for 0xf; sent after making a character, as captured

0xe465b0.name: ReadReply
0xe465b0.evidence: vtable slot 1: 0xf to 0xe408c0 and the done callback; any other opcode fails the step

0xe4fb00.name: ReadError
0xe4fb00.evidence: vtable slot 2 (inherited by the operations): for a body whose sequence @0 is the operation's, maps the error code @8 (1001.., 3000.., 5000..) to a class and reports it with the text @0x14

0xe3fc70.name: ReadServiceAccountList
0xe3fc70.evidence: body of 0xc: @8 0 or 1 clears the list, count @9, bytes @0xa/@0xb kept, then count 0x50-byte entries @0x10 copied into a vector

0xe410c0.name: ReadServerList
0xe410c0.evidence: body of 0x15: the list starts over when the u16 @0xa is 0; u16 count @0xc; 0x54-byte world entries @0x18, deduplicated on their u16 @2; returns bit 0 of @8 inverted (more pages)

0xe3fdf0.name: ReadCharaList
0xe3fdf0.evidence: body of 0xd: u16s @0x10/@0x12 and u32 @0xc kept (per-world limit, account slots, ...); (@8 & 0xfe) == 0 clears the list; count @9 entries of 0x450 bytes @0x18 built by CharaEntry; returns bit 0 of @8 inverted (more pages)

0xe40080.name: ReadCharaMakeReply
0xe40080.evidence: body of 0xe: with @9 non-zero, builds a CharaEntry from @0x10 and adds it (step 3 instead renames the entry whose content id matches @0x10/@0x14)

0xe3cb10.name: CharaEntry
0xe3cb10.evidence: builds a 0x468-byte character from a 0x450-byte packet entry (copied whole): content id @8, a byte @0x10 (low 6 bits), world id @0x18, name @0x1a; the text @0x4a is parsed through an istringstream into a ClientSelectData @0x460

0x904e60.name: WaitCharaSheets
0x904e60.evidence: registers a CallbackSheetWaiter (continuation 0x9018e0) with sheet 9 for one row per character (row 0 for an entry with content id 0); with no characters it never fires (traced: the continuation is not reached) and character select stays empty

0x9018e0.name: OnCharaSheetsLoaded
0x9018e0.evidence: the waiter's continuation: builds the 0x18-byte character list for the UI, then shows character select, or (state @0xfc == 8) the world list first (0x8ed740), as traced

0xcb8140.name: SheetRegisterWaiter
0xcb8140.evidence: sheet vtable slot 0x48 (traced from WaitCharaSheets): for each of the waiter's count items looks the row up and fires the waiter when loaded, queues it otherwise; a waiter with count 0 is neither fired nor queued

0x8a2540.name: CheckNewCharacter
0x8a2540.evidence: New Character: message 0x3c (no available character slots) unless a list holds fewer characters than the character list's u16 @0x12, 0x3d unless a world holds fewer than its u16 @0x10, else on to character creation (0x883080); seen in game with both at 0, then working at 8

0xba51d0.name: Dispatch
0xba51d0.evidence: vtable slot 1: switches on the IPC header's opcode @2 through a byte table @0xba6359+opcode (0x67..0x2eb) and calls one handler per case with the body (+0x10); InitZone 0x19a, spawn 0x190, ActorControl 0x142-0x144 (one handler, three argument sets) among them; the server's packets reached the handlers in game

0xc2fb20.name: ZoneClientUpdate
0xc2fb20.evidence: per frame: pulls each zone packet (via 0x1047bd0) and passes it to the game's receiver (+0x2a4, PacketDispatcher); answers down 0x19a with up 0x69 (FinishLoading, seen after InitZone) and uses down 0x65's @0x10 as the ping time; sends up 0x65 every 10 s; once the connection state is 4 or more calls the logout callback with (1, 10101) or (2, 90000) and tears the zone client down

0xab56a0.name: ReadInitZone
0xab56a0.evidence: the body of down 0x19a: territory u16 @2 loaded (with u32 @4), weather u8 @0xc for it, flags @0xd, four u16 @0xe, position f32 x3 @0x18; the client loaded territory 129 at the sent position

0xa55c00.name: HandleSpawn
0xa55c00.evidence: handler of down 0x190 (and 0x191-0x193 nearby): queues the body with the segment's source actor id (0xa5d350), clearing a slot first if the queue is full

0xa5d350.name: QueueSpawn
0xa5d350.evidence: copies the 0x288-byte body (0xa2 dwords) and the actor id into a 0x2a0-byte ring-buffer entry, read later by 0xa54ef0

0xa64860.name: CreateCharacter
0xa64860.evidence: makes character slot param_4 (0..99, body @0x2b) for actor id param_3; if it is the local actor id (DAT_01379690, the id game login gave) sets the local player (0xa9f360); seen: the local player pointer set after the server's spawn

0xa9f360.name: SetLocalPlayer
0xa9f360.evidence: DAT_01379694 = this, the pointer InitZone and the UI read as the local player

0xaac200.name: ReadSpawn
0xaac200.evidence: reads a 0x288-byte spawn body into a character: base id @4, slot @0x2b, status @0x2c, pose @0x2d, kind @0x30 (1 player, 2 battle NPC, 3 event NPC via 0xaaa870 with the base id), weapons u64 @0x48/0x50/0x58, rotation u16 @0x60, model @0x62, level @0x6a, class @0x6b, HP @0x6c, 30 statuses @0x98, name @0x208, customize[26] @0x228, models u32 x10 @0x244, position @0x26c; players and event NPCs sent this way appeared correctly

0xa51200.name: SendClientTrigger
0xa51200.evidence: builds up 0x191 (0x30 bytes): five u32 arguments @0..0x10 (a command id first; 0x0e and 0x02 seen) and sends it through the network module; ~150 callers across the game

0xc2bba0.name: SendLogout
0xc2bba0.evidence: sends up 0x263 (0x18 bytes, a flag @0) on the zone connection; reached from the menu's Logout through 0x975070; answered with down 0x2d6 the client logs out cleanly

0x433ab0.name: OnLogoutReply
0x433ab0.evidence: UIModule slot 31 kind 7 (down 0x2d6 through PacketDispatcher case 0x92): with logout pending (DAT_01372338) starts the logout (0x7e4b80) with a 60-frame countdown

0x7e4b80.name: BeginLogout
0x7e4b80.evidence: fades out and sets the lobby agent's state @0x68f to 0x12, whose countdown then calls 0x974760 → 0xc2e910; called by /logout (0x4781c0) and OnLogoutReply

0xc2e910.name: FinishLogout
0xc2e910.evidence: tears down the zone (+0x288) and chat (+0x28c) clients itself, then calls the logout callback (+0x2ac slot 1) with code 0; seen: no error dialog, back to the title

0x7e5140.name: OnLogout
0x7e5140.evidence: LogoutCallbackInterface slot 1 (vtable 0x10da704 in AgentLobby at +0x10): resets the game UI and keeps the logout codes @0x6dc/@0x6e0 for the title screen

0x882980.name: UpdateWorldList
0x882980.evidence: per world: counts characters with its id @0, then a status from its flags byte @4 (masks 1, 2 @0x13598ee/f, 4 @0x13598f2) and the per-world limit (ReadCharaList's u16 @0x10); flag 4 and room means a character can be made there
